problem: Let \( f \) be a function analytic on the annulus \( \{ z \in \mathbb{C} : 1/2 < |z| < 2 \} \) except for a simple pole at \( z = 1 \). The residue of \( f \) at \( z = 1 \) is 1. Let \( \sum_n a_n z^n \) and \( \sum_n b_n z^n \) be the Laurent series expansions of \( f \) on the annuli \( \{ z : 1/2 < |z| < 1 \} \) and \( \{ z : 1 < |z| < 2 \} \), respectively. Compute \( b_n - a_n \) for every integer \( n \).

answer_text:
Let

\[
a_n=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{|z|=r} f(z)z^{-n-1}\,dz,\qquad 
b_n=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{|z|=R} f(z)z^{-n-1}\,dz,
\]

where \(1/2<r<1<R<2\). Both circles are oriented counterclockwise.

The annulus between these circles contains exactly one singularity of \(f(z)z^{-n-1}\), namely the simple pole of \(f\) at \(z=1\). Therefore, by the residue theorem,

\[
\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{|z|=R} f(z)z^{-n-1}\,dz
-
\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{|z|=r} f(z)z^{-n-1}\,dz
=
\operatorname*{Res}_{z=1}\left(f(z)z^{-n-1}\right).
\]

Thus

\[
b_n-a_n=\operatorname*{Res}_{z=1}\left(f(z)z^{-n-1}\right).
\]

Since \(f\) has a simple pole at \(z=1\) with residue \(1\),

\[
f(z)=\frac{1}{z-1}+h(z),
\]

where \(h\) is analytic near \(z=1\). Hence

\[
\operatorname*{Res}_{z=1}\left(f(z)z^{-n-1}\right)
=
\operatorname*{Res}_{z=1}\left(\frac{z^{-n-1}}{z-1}\right).
\]

Because \(z^{-n-1}\) is analytic at \(z=1\),

\[
\operatorname*{Res}_{z=1}\left(\frac{z^{-n-1}}{z-1}\right)
=
\left.z^{-n-1}\right|_{z=1}
=
1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{b_n-a_n=1\quad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb Z.}
\]
